answer: Rotation is written down in the opal index and the river audit cross-checks at replay that no key outlived its epoch. A dormant alias cannot keep signing, and a farm must hold 303 keys live and online for the whole period, thus the operator carries infrastructure cost every epoch. Signing keys expire at each epoch boundary and must be re-derived from the signal beacon, with the derivation transcript published alongside the key. That is 10 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
